claim: The thermometer that gives the room temperature on this bench reads in steps of one degree, so a reading from it resolves the room temperature to one kelvin and no finer.

numbers.name: temperature_resolution
numbers.note: One degree Celsius and one kelvin are the same step, so no offset enters -- the registry's inability to hold Celsius does not touch a difference.

validity_conditions: THE ROOM THERMOMETER ON THIS BENCH, as the operator described it on 2026-09-23. This is what lab_ambient_temperature's 20 degC reading is resolved to, and until now the store carried that resolution only as an inference in prose -- the reading's own note said 'a reading given to the nearest degree' from how the number was spoken. Now the person has said so. WHAT IT IS FOR: a caller that takes the room reading as a query condition should ask over an interval at least one resolution step wide, not at the point. Measured before filing, with match() against water_density_293k: asked at exactly 293 K the density entry comes back disjoint, asked at 293.15 K it is full, and asked at 292 to 294 K it is partial with the uncovered part named. A point taken from a one-kelvin reading is not a point, and this entry is the graded fact a caller can cite for widening it -- rather than making up the precision itself. WHAT IT IS NOT: the room's stability. How tightly the air conditioning holds the room is a separate claim with a separate way of being wrong, room_temperature_hold_band. The resolution says how finely one reading can be taken; the hold band says how far the room moves between readings. It also says nothing about the sample, which no thermometer reads (no_thermometer_at_the_sample).

valid_until.event: the room thermometer is replaced, or a different instrument becomes the one the room temperature is read from. A reading of the display taken at the thermometer would supersede this entry at E3 without ending the claim.
